extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent examiners, and law students studying U.S. patent practice
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, statutory standards, and procedural guidance governing U.S. patent prosecution, reissue, appeals, enforcement (litigation/equity), disclaimers, patent extensions, fees, and design-patent formalities under the cited statute and accompanying treatise commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner rulemaking for affidavits and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in cases pending in the Patent Office, and such affidavits and depositions may be taken before any officer authorized by law to take depositions to be used in the courts of the United States, or of the State where the officer resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants the Commissioner authority to set procedures for obtaining testimonial evidence for contested Patent Office matters; contemplates use of officers competent for federal/state courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court clerk issuance of subpoenas for Patent Office proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The clerk of any court of the United States for any district or territory wherein testimony is to be taken for use in any contested case pending in the Patent Office shall, upon application, issue a subpoena for any witness residing or being within said district or territory, commanding him to appear and testify before any officer authorized to take depositions and affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism to compel witnesses via federal court process for Patent Office contested cases; failure to obey may be enforced or punished by the issuing judge on proof of neglect or refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fees, travel limits, and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Every witness duly subpoenaed and in attendance shall be allowed the same fees as are allowed to witnesses attending the courts of the United States, but no witness shall be required to attend at any place more than forty miles from the place where the subpoena is served unless fees and travel expenses (and one day's attendance) are paid or tendered at service; witness may refuse to disclose any secret invention or discovery owned by himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits compulsory attendance to 40 miles absent payment; ties witness compensation to federal rates; protects witnesses from compelled disclosure of their own secret inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal examiner decisions within Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant for a patent or reissue whose claims have been twice rejected, and every party to an interference, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner (or examiner in charge of interferences) to the board of examiners-in-chief, having once paid the fee for such appeal provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines internal appeal path: primary examiner -> board of examiners-in-chief; fee required; applies to reissue and interference contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from examiners-in-chief to the Commissioner in person
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party is dissatisfied with the decision of the examiners-in-chief, he may, on payment of the duty required by law, appeal to the Commissioner in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes next-step internal appeal to the Commissioner; payment of statutory duty required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Supreme Court of the District of Columbia
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party (except a party to an interference) is dissatisfied with the decision of the Commissioner, he may appeal to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, sitting in banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies external judicial review forum for Patent Office decisions (D.C. court) as next recourse after administrative appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of reasons of appeal and scope of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia the appellant shall give notice to the Commissioner and file in the Patent Office within such time as appointed his reasons of appeal, specifically set forth in writing; the court shall revise the decision in a summary way on the evidence produced before the Commissioner and the revision shall be confined to the points set forth in the reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specific written reasons of appeal and confines court review to those points and the administrative record; emphasizes summary review on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner duties on judicial appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: On receiving notice of appeal the Commissioner shall notify all parties who appear to be interested; the party appealing shall lay before the court certified copies of all original papers and evidence, and the Commissioner shall furnish the court with the grounds of his decision fully set forth in writing; Commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath as to principles of the machine or thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligates the Commissioner to compile and provide the administrative record, notify interested parties, and permit sworn explanation of technical principles when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remedy where patent application refused
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent on application is refused for any reason by the Commissioner or by the Supreme Court of D.C. upon appeal from the Commissioner, the applicant may have remedy by bill in equity; the court may adjudge the applicant is entitled to receive a patent for his invention, or part thereof, and may authorize the Commissioner to issue such patent on filing a copy of the adjudication and compliance with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an equitable backstop allowing courts to order issuance of a patent despite administrative refusal, subject to notice and usual equitable procedures; applicant bears costs where no opposing party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defective or insufficient specification or overclaiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective or insufficient specification, or because the patentee claimed more than he had right to claim, if the error arose by inadvertence, accident, or mistake and without fraudulent or deceptive intention, the Commissioner shall, on surrender of the patent and payment of duty, cause a new patent (reissue) to be issued in accordance with the corrected specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows reissue to correct inadvertent errors; requires surrender and fee; reissued patent relates to unexpired term and can be split into several patents for distinct parts on demand with separate reissue fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue limitations — no new matter, revision subject to original-application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter shall be introduced into the specification in a reissue; specifications and claim in every such case shall be subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original applications are. In case of machine patents the model or drawings may not be amended except each by the other; when there is neither model nor drawing, amendments may be made upon proof satisfactory to the Commissioner that such new matter or amendment was part of the original invention and omitted by inadvertence, accident, or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits introducing new subject-matter in reissues unless narrowly proven to have been part of original invention; subjects reissues to original-application scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial validity and disclaimer procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, through inadvertence, accident, or mistake and without fraudulent intention a patentee has claimed more than he was original inventor of, his patent shall be valid for all that part which is truly and justly his own provided it is a material or substantial part; the patentee (or heirs/assigns) may, on payment of duty, make disclaimer of such parts not chosen to be claimed, stating extent of interest; the disclaimer shall be in writing, attested by witnesses, and recorded in the Patent Office and thereafter be considered part of the original specification to the extent of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows curing overclaiming by recorded disclaimer; disclaimer is formal (writing, witnesses, recording) and becomes part of the record; does not affect pending actions except as to unreasonable neglect or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for patent suits and equitable relief
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under the patent laws shall be originally cognizable in equity as well as at law by the circuit courts of the United States, district courts having circuit powers, or by the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia or of any territory; courts may grant injunctions according to equity principles to prevent violation of patent rights on such terms as they deem reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies federal jurisdiction and equitable authority (including injunctions) for enforcement of patent rights; emphasizes court discretion on reasonable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages and enhancement in infringement decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon decree for infringement the claimant shall be entitled to recover, in addition to profits to be accounted for by the defendant, the damages the complainant has sustained thereby; the court shall assess the same and shall have the same powers to increase the damages in its discretion that are given to increase verdict damages; actions must be brought during the patent term or within six years after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits recovery of profits and actual damages, and discretionary enhancement up to statutory bounds; statute of limitations tied to patent term or six years post-expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to writ of error or appeal to U.S. Supreme Court
rubrics_metrics.description: A writ of error or appeal to the Supreme Court of the United States shall lie from all judgments and decrees of any circuit court, district court exercising circuit jurisdiction, or the Supreme Court of D.C. or of any territory, in any action or case touching patent rights, in the same manner and under the same circumstances as other judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves appellate review to the U.S. Supreme Court from patent judgments in lower federal courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Patent Office records as competent evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Written or printed copies of any records, books, papers, or drawings belonging to the Patent Office, and of letters-patent under the signature of the Commissioner with the seal of office affixed, shall be competent evidence in all cases wherein the originals could be evidence; copies of foreign letters-patent certified in like manner shall be prima facie evidence of the fact of granting and of the date and contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes use of certified copies of Patent Office records and foreign patent copies as admissible evidence; establishes prima facie status for foreign patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief against interfering patents by suit in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there shall be interfering patents any person interested in any one of such interfering patents or in the working of the invention claimed under either may have relief against the interfering patentee by suit in equity; the court may adjudge either of the patents void in whole or in part, or inoperative or invalid in any particular part of the United States according to the interest of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an equitable remedy to resolve interfering patents; effects limited to parties and those deriving title under them subsequent to judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions for infringement and permissible plaintiffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages for infringement may be recovered by action on the case in any circuit or appropriate district court, in the name of the party interested either as patentee, assignee, or grantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who may sue (patentee, assignee, grantee); allows actions in appropriate federal courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced judgment for plaintiff subject to verdict multiplier
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever in such action a verdict shall be rendered for the plaintiff the court may enter judgment thereon for any sum above the amount found by the verdict as the actual damages sustained, not exceeding three times the amount of such verdict, together with the costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authority to enter judgment in excess of verdict up to treble damages in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special defenses available under General Issue with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: In any action for infringement the defendant may plead the general issue and, having given written notice to the plaintiff or his attorney thirty days before trial, may prove any one or more special matters: (First) the specification was made to contain less than the whole truth or more than necessary to produce desired effect (fraudulent description); (Second) he had surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent for that which was in fact invented by another who was using reasonable diligence; (Third) it had been patented or described in some printed publication prior to his supposed invention; (Fourth) he was not the original and first inventor of any material and substantial part of the thing patented; (Fifth) it had been in public use or on sale in this country for more than two years before his application or had been abandoned to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the statutory defenses that a defendant may prove with proper notice; if any alleged special matter is found for defendant judgment shall be rendered for him with costs. Similar defenses apply in equity suits with like notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirement for prior-invention/knowledge proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: In notices as to proof of previous invention, knowledge, or use of the thing patented the defendant shall state the names of patentees and the dates of their patents and when granted, and the names and residences of the persons alleged to have invented or had prior knowledge, and where and by whom it had been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specificity in pleading prior art/prior use defenses (names, dates, places, actors) to enable effective proof and notice to plaintiff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith belief as to foreign prior use not fatal absent printed publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it appears that the patentee, at the time of making his application, believed himself to be the original and first inventor, the patent shall not be held void on account of the invention having been known or used in a foreign country before his invention, if it had not been patented or described in a printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a limited protection for applicants who in good faith believed themselves original despite foreign prior use, provided no prior printed publication/patent exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extension application timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring an extension of a patent issued prior to March 2, 1861 shall make written application to the Commissioner setting forth reasons why extension should be granted and furnish a written statement under oath of the ascertained value of the invention and his receipts and expenditures with sufficient detail to exhibit a true account of loss and profit; application must be filed not more than six months nor less than ninety days before expiration of the original term and no extension shall be granted after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies filing window (90–180 days pre-expiration), required sworn financial statement, and non-extendability after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and hearing procedure for extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of such application and payment of duty, the Commissioner shall publish notice in one newspaper in Washington and in other papers in the sections most interested adversely for at least sixty days prior to the day set for hearing; the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner of the class who shall report whether the invention was new and patentable when the original patent was granted; Commissioner shall hear and decide upon the evidence and if satisfied that the patentee without neglect failed to obtain reasonable remuneration and that extension is just and proper with due regard to the public interest, he shall make a certificate renewing and extending the patent for seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets notice, examiner referral, evidentiary hearing, and standards for granting a 7‑year extension (reasonable remuneration, absence of neglect, public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of extension to assignees and grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefit of the extension of a patent shall extend to the assignees and grantees of the right to use the thing patented to the extent of their interest therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension's benefits flow to those who hold rights in the patent to the extent of their interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory patent and ancillary fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates for patent fees: on filing each original application $15; issuing each original patent $20; filing each caveat $10; application for reissue $30; filing each disclaimer $10; application for extension $50; granting of every extension $50; first appeal from primary examiners to examiners-in-chief $10; appeal from examiners-in-chief to Commissioner $20; certified copies 10 cents per hundred words; recording assignments/agreements/powers of attorney/other paper: up to 300 words $1, up to 1000 words $2, over 1000 words $3; copies of drawings at reasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed statutory fee amounts for various prosecution and administrative actions; use to compute required payments for filings, appeals, reissue, disclaimers, extensions, and copy/recording fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and refund of Patent Office fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees may be paid to the Commissioner or to the Treasurer or any assistant treasurers or designated depositaries; all money received shall be paid into the treasury without deduction; the Treasurer is authorized to pay back sums paid through mistake upon certificate from the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes acceptable payees, treatment of receipts, and refund process for mistaken payments requiring Commissioner's certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-patent eligibility and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has invented or produced any new and original design for a manufacture, bust, statue, alto-relievo or bas-relief, new and original design for printing of fabrics, new original impression/ornament/pattern/print/picture to be printed or otherwise on articles of manufacture, or any new useful and original shape or configuration of any article of manufacture not known or used before may, upon payment of duty and other due proceedings had, obtain a patent therefor. The Commissioner may dispense with models of designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by drawings or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends patent protection to ornamentation, patterns, and shapes; permits drawings/photos instead of models when adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-patent term choices and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs may be granted for three years and six months, or for seven years, or for fourteen years as the applicant may elect; fees for designs: 3.5 years $10; 7 years $15; 14 years $30; for other cases fees same as inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant elects term for design patent and pays corresponding statutory fee; other prosecution fees align with invention fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and abandonment time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications verified by oath; an application is abandoned unless completed within two years (as noted in index entries); filing formalities and timing are crucial for maintaining application viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From index entries: emphasizes verification, time-to-completion rules and abandonment consequences—practical prosecution constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting — object and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of a claim is not to aid the description but to ascertain what is claimed as new; it must be a means of clearly presenting the subject-matter of the patent, must distinguish between the old and new, need not describe in detail what is old, and must not be for an abstract principle but for a principle embodied in a particular organism or machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides claim drafting: claims should define the novel scope, avoid abstract formulation, distinguish old from new, and be sufficiently concrete to identify the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity in description or claim is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguity in the description of the invention is fatal; ambiguity of claim is distinguishable from want of clear and sufficient description and may be produced by introduction of things unnecessary or misuse of terms; ambiguous claims covering a whole class of subjects where only one answers are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that unclear descriptions/claims can invalidate or defeat enforceability; avoid unnecessary elements and imprecise terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and reissue restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of amendment by disclaimer, surrender and reissue, and other procedures does not authorize surrender of valid patents for fraudulent purposes; amendment may give an invalid patent validity and is subject to the same restrictions as original applications; right of amendment applies to extended patents as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments/reissues are limited tools — must not be used fraudulently; reissues may cure defects but are constrained by statutory and equitable limits.
